# A6. Cube draft-and-build reads

**A6.1 Authority and signature.** The research lead signs this declaration before D8's A/A, before D11, and before any A6 games, including doses and D14 sizing. The 24 November engineering acceptance supplies the rulings. A1, A2 and A4 r3 apply with their final decisions. A6 fills their deferred read rules and amends A4.5 and A4.6. A4.5 permits the stated builder as a measurement baseline in early and acceptance (a), the D8 A/A, (b'), D13, and D14's probes for early and acceptance (a) and for (c), in addition to (c) itself. Those uses are outside training. A4.6 keeps the role-swapped chairs, cross pairings and pair unit. The 2 by 2 in A6.10 replaces the single builder row and gives 64 games per pair. In this declaration, the early pod has its own read (a). Acceptance requires a win in acceptance (a) and (b), and non-inferiority in (c) for the learned builder. The early pod requires a win in early (a).

Research lead, signature and time: **TO FILL AT SIGNING**. A6 revision and hash, signed D0, signed A1/A2/A4 revision, and provisional binary, cube list, fence, pool, registry, index and table pins: **TO FILL AT SIGNING**. Record the D7 reader revision and fixture receipts before D8. Later pin fields below are filled in the named manifests when those artifacts exist. No later pin or D14 result changes a rule signed here.

## Common rules

**A6.2 Policies and inputs.** In each acceptance game the frozen M3 gate pilot plays both sides. In early (a) and its companions, checkpoint X plays both sides. X and the candidate come from D11's predeclared early read mark. The acceptance candidate comes from D11's predeclared acceptance mark. A draft uses sampled release picks and builds at temperature 1 with the signed M4 sampler. Uniform picks use `UniformSeatPicker`. The stated build uses A1.6 `StatedSeatBuilder`. The pilot uses the mode certified by M3 and bound in D11, including the wide sampler and any signed keep offset. A candidate, pilot, or mode is fixed across both looks. D8 uses uniform legal play and D0's provisional inputs. M5 uses D15's requalified inputs. The D11 and read manifests record the marks, decoding identities and settings, binary, card database, pool, fence, index, table, layout, candidate, and pilot pins, including A5's checkpoint, after-state, training math, table binding and source binary fields: **TO FILL AT SIGNING** of the applicable manifests. Future checkpoint hashes are bound to the declared marks as those checkpoints are created.

**A6.3 Scores and denominators.** A natural win scores 1, a natural draw 1/2 and a natural loss 0, from the focal side's perspective. The other side scores the complement. There is one scheduled attempt per game. Use the natural result and its session-player order from the pod record. A halt has no observed score. Drop it from the completed-game denominator of its pool or builder row. If that mean has no completed game, it is absent. For a difference needing two means, both must exist. A draft in (b), (b') or (c) averages its available pool statistics with equal weight. A pair in (a) has one statistic per builder row and needs both rows for the interaction. Average the defined draft or pair statistics with equal weight. A unit with no defined statistic is omitted for that statistic and counted. Report planned and observed units, games, complete and empty pools or rows, and their exact denominators, by statistic and look. A2.3's halt and game-length breakdowns apply. Report the A2.1 warning if more than 0.1% of completed games exceed 8,192 driver decisions.

**A6.4 Intervals.** Order the n planned clusters by draft or pair index. For each b from 0 through 9,999, draw n indices with replacement in pure Python, using `seed(["bootstrap", namespace, b, t]) mod n` for t from 0 through n minus 1. Use the same index draws for every statistic and halt treatment of that read and look. Resample whole clusters. Recompute the statistic using the resampled defined unit scores, retaining multiplicities and skipping absent scores for the drop statistic. If the observed statistic or any of its 10,000 resamples is undefined, its drop interval is undefined. Report that diagnostic and void a gate whose primary interval is undefined. Every imputed statistic uses the full planned slots and units. Sort each set of resampled values. Take the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles by linear interpolation at p times 9,999, with p equal to 1/40 and 39/40. Compute scores, means and threshold comparisons as rational quantities, including interpolation, before rounding for display. A run with every game halted is void. Read (b') uses (c)'s bootstrap index draws. The second look draws from the pooled planned clusters of both looks.

**A6.5 Signed halt completions and voids.** Report the drop statistic and interval, and two sensitivity statistics and intervals using the same resampling scheme. For the lower completion, substitute a loss for a halt whose focal score enters the statistic with a positive coefficient and a win where it enters with a negative coefficient. Reverse these substitutions for the upper completion. Keep natural results fixed. These substitutions use every planned game at its planned weight. They enter only the sensitivity calculation. For each resample the full-denominator statistic lies between those two completions for any assignment of halted games, and the percentile endpoints inherit that ordering. Apply the same decision cut to the drop, lower and upper intervals. A gate is void if these three verdicts differ, including when one is inconclusive. A win must therefore survive the lower completion, and a loss or inferiority must survive the upper completion. A report without a cut shows both completions and flags an undefined drop interval. A/A has the stricter exact test in A6.12.

**A6.6 Looks and disposition.** For (a), early (a) and (b), the null for a win is that the statistic is at or below its decision cut. For (c), the null for non-inferiority is that the difference is at or below its negative margin. At a look, the lower percentile must be strictly above the cut to win or show non-inferiority. If the upper percentile is strictly below the cut, declare loss of the gate, or inferiority in (c). All other valid cases are inconclusive. Equality stays inconclusive. The one-sided level for a win is 0.025 per look, for a total nominal level of 0.05 per gate by Bonferroni. The lower-side decision uses the symmetric cut rule. This is a per-gate allocation. A win ends that gate. A loss or inferiority ends the attempt. For early (a), the attempt is the early label read. An inconclusive first look gets one read-only extension of **2n fresh clusters**, starting at the next unused index. The second look uses all **3n clusters**. The candidate, pilot, seeds already used, and all constants are held fixed. A second inconclusive or a second-look void ends the attempt. A first-look halt-void supplies no verdict. See Open for the lead for its disposition. A2.5 governs an interruption for a fix, as specified in A6.7. Any new attempt after a result requires a fresh holdout and a pre-data signed A6 amendment. After the acceptance gates end an acceptance attempt, any later training requires separate lead authorization. No holdout, companion, dose or panel result sets a training constant, stop point, decoder or checkpoint choice.

**A6.7 Stops and custody.** Pass A2.1's 16,384 driver, 16,384 physical and 32,768 policy-step caps and 600 s watchdog explicitly. Set `max_replays` to 0. A watchdog expiry voids the batch or look as infrastructure failure. Rerun it once with its original seeds on the same platform. If the rerun expires on any game, stop. A repeat expiry for the same game is a hang and contributes no game score. If the rerun expires on a different game, record both game IDs and report the read as a void infrastructure failure with no third run. The attempt then ends; it does not restart at unused indices, and any new attempt needs a new declaration. Apply A2.5 to each read as a whole window in logical order, with its pinned completed baseline. For a prospective second look, the read window is the pooled games. Count each scheduled game once, and report stop-kind rates over all games in the window and charged card rates over games containing that card. Process death or hang fires immediately. A completed read stands on its build. A read interrupted by a tripwire fix is void and starts again at the next unused index of its namespace on the new pins and applicable replacement baseline. Retire the unused indices already reserved in the interrupted plan. For an interrupted shared prefix, retire its overlapping plan on that build and start any still-unfinished reads at the same next unreserved draft index. Use that index in their game keys. Completed reads stand on their original build and share no drafts with the restarted looks. D0 records whether Q9 suspends the baseline-rate triggers in the labelled shakedown until the census exists. A6's symmetry and halt-void criteria still apply.

**A6.8 Seed and record contract.** Use `m4-interfaces/v1` and `mtg-kernel-cube-pod-record/v1`. For the first attempt use run `v1`. Indices are zero-based. For seed-source namespace `ns` and unit index `i`, the default plan keys are `draft_seed = seed([ns,"draft",run,i])`, `pod_seed = seed([ns,"pod",run,i])` and, where applicable, `league_seed = seed([ns,"league",run,i])`. Use the seed sources and indices declared below. Use the interface's picker streams. Use `build = 0` for a candidate or current build and `build = 1` for its stated counterpart. The stated builder consumes no randomness. Shared candidate builds of the same pool use build 0 in all reads that reference them. `seed` is the pinned `deal.py` compact-JSON SHA-256, first eight bytes little-endian, masked to 63 bits. The A6 namespaces are listed below. They are disjoint from training, census, calibration and owner views. Each is allocated once to its plan. Declared overlap is limited to paired schedules, companions' pack seeds, the shared draft prefix for (b), (b') and (c), the shared (b') and (c) outcomes, and fixed panels replayed as declared. Extension consumes unused indices. A2.1's watchdog rerun preserves seeds, and A2.5's post-fix restart consumes unused indices. A1.5's frozen dealer formulas are exempt from kind tags.

For reads, A6 proposes to read the scheduled-game instruction in section 4 of `m4-interfaces/v1`, “take their game seed and seats from the read's plan,” as allowing the plan to supply `draft_seed` and `pod_seed` explicitly. The record's `namespace` is the game namespace. The plan names the seed-source namespace for each seed and supplies the two values. For mirrors it supplies the parent pair's seeds. For companions it supplies the parent pack seed and the companion pod seed. For (b) and (c) it supplies both from `read-gate-pools`. D5 must take these two seeds from the read plan. Keep the pod-j derivation for training. The lead must confirm this reading of v1 or issue v2 before it is used.

**A6.9 Record validation and coupled shuffles.** Read u64 fields exactly. Match each record to its frozen plan by namespace, run, pod index, seeds, pins, pilot, caps, draft, chair policy, and deck and game IDs. Record both pod IDs of an (a) pair in the plan, using `pod_index = 2i+r` for mirror r, with both records taking the shared seed values that the plan derives with `i`. Validate those values against the plan. The plan also maps shared draft IDs and analysis families to their records. Records use `read_a` for (a), A/A and companions, `read_b` for (b), `paired_build` for the games of (b') and (c), `dose` for doses, `sizing` for D14, and `test` for fixtures. For paired builds check ordered matching via `paired_builds` deck IDs, opponent IDs and `games_x`/`games_y`. Read `games` and `attempts` in logical order and reconcile `halts`, `status` and `stop`. Fail validation on duplicate, missing or unexpected slots, invalid score pairs, a score on a halt, a replay attempt, a pin mismatch, or an incomplete record without an accounted-for stop. An unplayed slot is a technical interruption. It supplies no halt imputation.

Write every deck in canonical form as 40 one-card rows in ascending registry ID. A paired build uses its counterpart's scheduled seat, game seed, episode, env stream and action stream. It faces the identical opponent deck and row order. For games against C(P), this preserves the opponent's opening library and the permutation of 40 positions. The focal cards occupy the same opening positions when their canonical row indices agree. Later mulligans and play may diverge. Set `seat_rule` to `schedule`. The plan resolves the ordered-chair coin before seating or substituting decks in (a). On scheduled games the env and action seeds are `derive_seed(G, GameEnv, 0)` and `derive_seed(G, GameActions, 0)` for game seed G. A1.5 retains its own game seeds, episode mapping and seats. Compare its expanded libraries and initial hands to a frozen A1.5 episode before using the reader.

## Gate and companion reads

**A6.10 Acceptance (a).** Measure the edge of learned over uniform picks with the builder the seats would ship. Use `read-gate-a`. One unit is a role-swapped pair of pods on one pack seed and one pod seed. In pod 0 the learned seats are even. In pod 1 they are odd. Each pod drafts once. Build each pool with the candidate builder and with the stated builder. Within a builder row, both sides use that row's builder. Play the 16 learned-versus-uniform chair pairings in each pod under each builder. In `pod_pairings()` order, take G from `game_seed(pod_seed,g)` and bind `GameCoin` to the ordered chair IDs of pairing g before building the seat schedule. Use g as the episode index. Share G and this schedule across pods and builder rows. Both decks can change between builder rows. The unit has 64 planned games, 32 per builder row. It is the bootstrap cluster.

The four cells are focal scores for learned and uniform picks under each of the two builders. In each row calculate the learned score minus the uniform score as `2 * mean(learned score) - 1`. Thus the candidate-row edge, stated-row edge and their interaction are all in signed win-fraction difference units. Equality is zero on this scale. The required decision margin above equality is +0.04. The win null is edge at most +0.04. The cut +0.04 corresponds to a learned score of 0.52. The candidate row alone gives the verdict. Report the other row and the interaction, candidate edge minus stated edge, with intervals and both completions. The lower completion for either row takes every halt as a loss for the learned side. The lower interaction completion gives the learned side losses in the candidate row and wins in the stated row. Upper completions reverse those signs. Give the row and interaction denominators separately. Apply A6.3 to A6.7 and size by A6.18. Run the (a) fixtures of A6.20 at both pilot bindings, including the chair and builder switches.

**A6.11 Early-pod (a).** Measure the same edge under X at the D11 read mark. Use `read-early-a` and its own D14 pilot and spread. Apply all of A6.10's layout, pair clustering, scores, contrasts, +0.04 cut, halts, looks and tests to this separate namespace. A win permits the early pod label, “Drafted by a model that beat random picks with its learned builder. Play by checkpoint X.” The early result carries only that claim for this pilot and alternating-chair layout. Its companions describe other compositions. Early (a) and acceptance (a) retain separate holdouts and results even if X is the gate checkpoint. The result of early (a) decides only whether the early pod is labelled. It never stops, pauses, extends or changes M5. The acceptance candidate stays at D11's predeclared acceptance mark regardless of the early result. If D11's early read mark falls before K1 ends, freeze X and the candidate at that mark. The early holdout waits for the final K1 snapshot, its D14 sizing under X and the recording of its count under A6.19.

**A6.12 D8 A/A.** Check role attribution on four fixed pairs, indices 0 to 3, in `read-d8-aa`, before any decision read. Use A6.10's 64-game layout, provisional D0 pins and uniform pilot. Both pick labels use the identical uniform picker and the same per-chair stream in both pods. The candidate row uses the pinned `UniformFourStepBuilder` from section 2 of `m4-interfaces/v1` and the same build stream by chair in each mirror. The stated row uses A1.6 in both. For every corresponding chair pairing, assert equality of packs, pools, decks, scheduled chairs and seats, seeds and natural outcome in session-player order across the mirrors. Assert complementary focal scores and exactly zero edge for every pair in each builder row and zero interaction. A natural draw counts as 1/2. This is an exact zero null with zero tolerance, one fixed look, 256 planned games and no extension or sizing input. Report the drop scores and both signed completions by pair and row. A halt passes the game-level symmetry check only if the same game halts in both mirrors with the same stop kind, last-action source and decision counts. Exclude that game from both mirrors' completed-game denominators. An unmirrored halt or a mismatch in any of those fields fails the test. The signed completions are diagnostic. A row with no completed mirrored games has no edge and cannot certify the pair. A mismatch in a complete test is a failure. A void or failure blocks the symmetry receipt and goes to the lead. Only the technical recovery in A6.7 or a pre-data amendment for a new test permits another live attempt. Also run the planted asymmetric and non-zero-variance fixtures in A6.20. D15 repeats the reader fixtures on the frozen bindings.

**A6.13 Acceptance (b).** Measure the combined learned drafter and builder against the frozen A1.5 baseline. All eight chairs use learned picks and the candidate builder. The draft is the cluster. Each candidate build D plays four games against its A1.5 opponent dealt from the active pool minus D's nonbasic cards. A pool statistic is D's mean score over four planned slots. A draft has eight such pools and 32 planned games. The statistic is the mean of the draft scores on the [0,1] win-fraction scale. No edge is 0.50. The decision margin is +0.02 and the win null is score at most 0.52. For the lower completion count each halt as a loss for D. For the upper count it as a win. Apply A6.3 to A6.7. Use namespace `read-gate-b`, run `v1` and A1.5 dealer index `8i+s` for draft i and chair s. Use `read-gate-b` as the bootstrap namespace in A6.4. Use A1.5's four distinct game seeds and its own schedule, two on the play and two on the draw. For the four games in A1.5 slot order, pass A1.5's own u64 episode values if its frozen function defines them, and otherwise the values 0, 1, 2 and 3, respectively. Store the same values in the record. Full frozen dealer key, game seed formula and seat schedule quoted from signed A1.5 and its merge commit: **TO FILL AT SIGNING**. Use the `read-gate-pools` draft prefix in A6.16. Use D14 and A6.18 for its own count. Run the frozen-dealer and scoring fixtures of A6.20.

**A6.14 Acceptance companion (b').** Measure learned pools through the fixed A1.6 builder against C(P). Use the stated-build games of (c) and all eight learned pools of each of its drafts. Score the stated build's mean in its four slots, with 32 planned games per draft. Report the mean across draft clusters on the [0,1] win-fraction scale, with 0.50 as the neutral reference. There is no null test, margin or decision cut. Report the drop interval and the stated-side loss and win completions through the clustered interval. A wholly halted report is void. An undefined drop interval is marked as such. Inherit (c)'s first-look count and any extension and report at each available (c) look. There is no independent spread, extension or inconclusive action. The number is specific to C(P). The (b) comparator is A1.5. Use A6.20's shared-outcome and sign tests.

**A6.15 Acceptance (c).** Check non-inferiority of the learned builder to the stated builder on the same learned pools. Play four games per build against C(P) on coupled schedules. For each pool, take the mean score of the candidate build minus that of the stated build. The draft averages the eight pool differences and is the bootstrap cluster. There are 64 planned games per draft, 4 per build per pool. Give equal weight to draft means. The signed win-fraction difference has equality at zero and margin 0.02. The non-inferiority null is difference at most -0.02. The decision cut is -0.02, using A6.6. For the lower completion take candidate halts as candidate losses and stated halts as stated wins. Reverse for the upper completion. Apply A6.3 to A6.7. Use `read-gate-c` for opponent and game schedules and for bootstrapping, with (b') sharing its stated results. Use A6.18 to record `n_c` drafts and `2*n_c` fresh drafts for any extension. Check the opponent, coupling, paired difference and void fixtures in A6.20.

**A6.16 Shared drafts and composition companions.** Reads (b) and (c) use the first `n_b` and `n_c` drafts of `read-gate-pools`, respectively. Both read plans take `draft_seed` and `pod_seed` from `read-gate-pools` and thus use the same learned pools and candidate builds on overlap. Their records carry their own game namespaces, `read-gate-b` and `read-gate-c`, respectively. Read (b') uses (c)'s prefix. Reserve `3*n_b` and `3*n_c` positions on the common draft stream and the corresponding game keys before any holdout games. A read's extension starts at its own first unused index on that prefix. Its outcomes and opponents stay in its separate game namespace. Use one plan, independent of observed verdicts, for this cross-read overlap.

For early and acceptance (a), also report A4.7's two compositions on `n_a` first-look pack seeds of the relevant (a). Use `read-early-a-one`, `read-early-a-all`, `read-gate-a-one` and `read-gate-a-all`. Each companion plan names its parent read as the source of `draft_seed`. It reuses only the first-look pack seeds and records its own game namespace. For one learned seat, rotate it through chairs 0 to 7, giving eight pods per seed. Use distinct pod seeds `seed([ns,"pod",run,i,r])` for rotation r, and `pod_index = 8i+r`. Play its seven cross games in each rotation, 56 per cluster. Score the learned edge as in (a), with both signed completions and draft-seed intervals. For all-learned, use one pod on each pack seed and its own pod seed. Play all 28 games and report completion, halts and game length. Use the candidate builder and the relevant read pilot for both compositions. Use `game_seed(pod_seed,g)` and the ordered-chair coin for seats. Apply A6.7. These companions have no decision cut or extension. They describe different tables and do not substitute for the gate.

## Common opponent and development measurements

Section 9c of `src/M4-DESIGN.md` fixes this dealer key without a run field. A6 exempts this key from the run field. Its single-use namespace identifies the plan. Draw 2 colours, 23 eligible nonland spells, 3 nonbasic lands and 7 basics of each drawn colour. Basics may be shared. If a draw is short, fail the plan and report the input. No fallback draws or substituted pools. Use the separately pinned common-opponent function. A1.5 remains pinned separately. The four games for opponent 0 use `G = seed([ns,"game",run,i,s,0,j])` for j from 0 to 3. Put the focal deck on the play at even j and on the draw at odd j, with session player 0 starting. Use j as the episode index within the pool and opponent. The plan uses distinct game IDs within each pod. Both builds use the same schedule and C(P).

## Sizing and reader checks

**A6.18 D14 sizing.** Use the final K1 snapshot identified by its declared update, frozen before sizing, as the non-identical probe. Before D14 record its hash, each probe plan and each read pilot pin. In sizing (a), use K1 picks against uniform with both builder rows as in (a), with K1 as the candidate builder. Probe under X in `size-early-a` and under the gate in `size-gate-a`, 48 pairs each. For (b), use 96 K1 drafts with K1 builds against the A1.5 opponent in `size-gate-b`. Use that namespace for the probe's A1.5 keys, with A6.13's run, dealer index and episode slots. For (c), use 48 K1 drafts with K1 versus stated builds against C(P) in `size-gate-c`. The gate pilot plays both. Each campaign measures 3,072 games and uses its gate's exact unit statistic, schedules and drop rules. Read (b') inherits (c)'s count. Report its own descriptive spread from the stated half of (c)'s sizing games. D14 seeds, decks and outcomes are excluded from holdouts. A probe with every unit identical by construction in a required contrast is invalid. With fewer than two defined observed units, an invalid probe, an incomplete plan, or an infrastructure or tripwire stop, D14 supplies no count until the probe is valid under the technical recovery rule or a pre-data amendment. Halted games in a completed probe are dropped and ledgered. Report the spread and number of defined units under drop and both signed completions.

Use the sample standard deviation `s` of the defined drop unit statistics, with denominator `m-1` for m defined units. For each valid probe with positive finite s and all units defined, compute `n_raw = ((1.96 + 0.84) * s / Delta)^2`, round up to a whole pair or draft, then clamp to [128,512]. For rounding, compute the equivalent `n_raw = (14/5)^2 * s_squared / Delta^2` from the exact sample variance. The design target is 80% first-look power at the specified alternative, using the normal approximation. For the two (a) reads, `Delta = 0.06` in signed edge units, for an alternative of +0.10 against +0.04. For (b), `Delta = 0.03`, for a mean of 0.55 against 0.52. For (c), `Delta = 0.02`, for equality against -0.02. If a valid probe has zero spread, or a valid completed probe has some undefined units but at least two defined, use the cap of 512 and flag the reason. A non-finite spread is a probe error. Disclose the floor or cap when it binds and report the approximate power at the selected count when s is positive and finite. Neither missing observations nor budget repricing changes these rules. For (c), report the pool and draft spreads and within-draft correlation as diagnostics. The draft spread goes directly into the formula.

## Consistency check of the signed halt-void rule

Decision 2 in the signature resolves the open disposition in A6.6. A first look with a defined primary interval and differing drop, lower and upper verdicts is void for the gate verdict and counts as inconclusive for scheduling. It gets the one declared read-only extension of 2n fresh clusters. A second-look void ends the attempt. An undefined primary interval at the first look also ends the attempt.

A6.6 says, “At a look, the lower percentile must be strictly above the cut to win or show non-inferiority.” It also says, “If the upper percentile is strictly below the cut, declare loss of the gate, or inferiority in (c).” The next sentences are “All other valid cases are inconclusive.” and “Equality stays inconclusive.” These sentences classify each of the three intervals. A shared verdict governs when all three agree. A verdict flip invokes the signed disposition, including when equality at a cut makes one of the three verdicts inconclusive.

A6.6 says, “A win ends that gate.” and “A loss or inferiority ends the attempt.” These actions require agreement across the three verdicts. A first-look drop win, loss or inferiority that flips under a completion takes the extension if the primary interval is defined.

A6.6 says, “An inconclusive first look gets one read-only extension of **2n fresh clusters**, starting at the next unused index.” and “The second look uses all **3n clusters**.” This includes a first-look verdict-flip void with a defined primary interval. The extension pools the first n clusters with the 2n fresh clusters. “A second inconclusive or a second-look void ends the attempt.” agrees with the signature.

A6.6 says, “A first-look halt-void supplies no verdict.” A verdict flip supplies no gate verdict, but the signature assigns it an inconclusive disposition for scheduling. “See Open for the lead for its disposition.” points to a decision that has now been made. Under Open for the lead, “Decide what a first-look halt-void does to the attempt.” is resolved. “Recommend ending the attempt without a second look, including when dropping halted games makes the primary interval undefined.” conflicts with the signed rule for a first-look verdict flip. The recommendation to end the attempt when the first-look primary interval is undefined agrees with the signature.

A6.6 says, “For early (a), the attempt is the early label read.” A6.11 says, “It never stops, pauses, extends or changes M5.” The extension for a verdict flip in early (a) applies only to that label read. A6.6 also says, “Any new attempt after a result requires a fresh holdout and a pre-data signed A6 amendment.” The extension is the second look of the same attempt. An attempt that ends is subject to the fresh-holdout and amendment rule.

A6.4 says, “If the observed statistic or any of its 10,000 resamples is undefined, its drop interval is undefined.” It then says, “Report that diagnostic and void a gate whose primary interval is undefined.” and “A run with every game halted is void.” For a gate, an undefined primary interval ends the attempt at either look. An all-halted gate run has an undefined primary interval and ends the attempt.

A6.5 says, “Apply the same decision cut to the drop, lower and upper intervals.” It then says, “A gate is void if these three verdicts differ, including when one is inconclusive.” and “A win must therefore survive the lower completion, and a loss or inferiority must survive the upper completion.” These sentences govern the validity of the gate verdict. The signature supplies the next action for a verdict-flip void at each look.

A6.7 says, “A watchdog expiry voids the batch or look as infrastructure failure.” It also says, “If the rerun expires on a different game, record both game IDs and report the read as a void infrastructure failure with no third run.” and “A read interrupted by a tripwire fix is void and starts again at the next unused index of its namespace on the new pins and applicable replacement baseline.” These technical voids follow A6.7, as does A6.6’s “A2.5 governs an interruption for a fix, as specified in A6.7.” A6.7’s “A6's symmetry and halt-void criteria still apply.” carries decision 2 into any gate look that completes under the recovery rules.

A6.5 says, “A/A has the stricter exact test in A6.12.” A6.12 says, “This is an exact zero null with zero tolerance, one fixed look, 256 planned games and no extension or sizing input.” and “A void or failure blocks the symmetry receipt and goes to the lead.” The signed verdict-flip extension applies to gates with decision cuts. A/A follows its exact test and technical recovery rules.

A6.5 says, “A report without a cut shows both completions and flags an undefined drop interval.” A6.14 says, “A wholly halted report is void.” and “An undefined drop interval is marked as such.” It also says, “Inherit (c)'s first-look count and any extension and report at each available (c) look.” and “There is no independent spread, extension or inconclusive action.” The descriptive void or undefined interval in (b') supplies no scheduling action. When a first-look verdict flip extends (c), (b') reports on the inherited second look.

A6.20 says in the (b) fixture, “Check that the lower completion voids the win.” In the (c) fixture it says, “The drop verdict is non-inferior and the read is void under the signed rule.” Both fixtures have defined primary intervals and differing verdicts, so each extends at a first look and ends the attempt at a second look. The common fixture sentences “Assert the first inconclusive schedules 2n new units and pools exactly 3n.” and “The second ends the attempt.” cover ordinary inconclusives and must also cover the signed disposition of verdict-flip voids.

For (c), the drop verdict is non-inferior and the read is void because the verdicts differ.
